rr6-nx: package notes, what to test on the console
==================================================

Nothing in this package has run on real hardware. Everything below was seen on the PC or in Ryujinx, which are proxies.

Install
-------
Copy COPY_TO_SD_switch_rr6-nx to sdmc:/switch/rr6-nx. Extract your disc into game_root (not the ISO itself).
DLC is optional: put the packages under dlc/, in any folders. The first start then extracts about 1.9 GB next to your saves, so the
first boot takes longer and needs the space.

The wedges: fixed (2026-11-03 evening, rr6_strip_markers)
----------------------------------------------------------
The streaked and huge black polygons in the course intro, and the wrong polygon on the rock wall, were the renderer's: the game's meshes
are triangle strips with 0xFFFF restart markers, and the draw path used until a mesh's whole-buffer copy exists counted the marker as a
vertex. On deko3d that ran each strip on through its cuts, with the cut's vertex read as zeros (a triangle to the object's origin). The PC
never showed it (Direct3D 12 cuts at 0xFFFF whatever the index width), and the emulator showed it only for a frame or two after each
camera cut. Ryujinx with the shipped settings now shows 0 bad frames in 364 burst captures through the intro and the race. Please confirm
on the console: the intro's three shots (tower, bridge, palms) and the race's first lap. It should also be faster: those draws converted
65536 vertices each before. In renut_ab.toml it is target 77: the off half brings the wedges back.

Point sprites fixed (2026-11-04 04:45)
--------------------------------------
The host geometry shaders that draw the game's point sprites had their vertex layout one slot off from the recompiled
shaders (a fog interpolator was added to those and not to these). On the PC every point-sprite pipeline failed to
link and the draws were skipped; on the console they linked silently with the sprite's size and texture coordinate
read from the wrong slots: a flat-coloured quad of a wrong size. If the hard rectangles in the sky were point sprites,
they are gone now; anything the game draws as points (glows, sparks, sun, lens flares) may appear for the first time.

Console tests: the chrome car and the black video screen
--------------------------------------------------------
Still console-only: the chrome car paint (hard white and black patches, plates blown out, opponents too) and the black video screen on
the tower. Ryujinx and the PC draw both right. The first suspect is now GPU ordering: the reflection map is drawn, resolved, warped into
six cube faces and sampled by the car, and the tower's video is a texture uploaded every frame; Ryujinx runs each draw's work to the end
before the next, the console's GPU does not. tests/ holds renut.toml with suspects switched off (or waits switched on). The NRO reads only
renut.toml, so copy a test over it, then race the first course and look at the car and the tower screen.
  test6_gpu_waits.toml             run this first: the GPU waits for idle at every render-to-texture hand-over and before every clear
                                   (banjo_deko3d_read_wait, _write_wait, _clear_wait). Slower; if the car goes right, one of the three is it
  test7_gpu_all_safe.toml          the waits plus Zcull, depth compression, barrier merging, lean barriers and the cached upload ring off,
                                   and rr6_frames_ahead 0: everything the console's GPU does and Ryujinx does not emulate
  test8_full_barriers.toml         the heaviest hammer: every barrier waits for the whole GPU, copy engine included, and drops every
                                   cache. Very slow. If the car is still chrome here, GPU ordering is ruled out for good
  test1_all_suspects_off.toml      the earlier set: tests 2-5 at once
  test2_clip_plane_off.toml        the reflection fix, rr6_user_clip_plane. The car should go matte
  test3_copies_off.toml            the machine copies, banjo_cpu_native_bulk
  test4_uniform_branches_off.toml  a shader compiler optimisation. Its shaders compile on the console, so expect a slower first race
  test5_frames_ahead_0.toml        the game waits for the render thread each frame, rr6_frames_ahead
  test9_texture_dump.toml          not a fix test: a recording. In six windows (120 s after launch, then every 40 s; two frames each)
                                   the textures the car's paint draw samples (the normal map, the six reflection faces, every mip
                                   level) are copied out of the GPU as the draw sees them and written to texture_dump/ next to the
                                   NRO (a few MB per frame; a short stall at each window). The garage, the car select and the race all
                                   count, so go straight to a race and be in it by about 3 minutes after launch. Send the folder
                                   with the logs: tools/texture_dump_view.py pictures them against the emulator's
  test10_no_color_compression.toml colour render targets without the GPU's hardware compression (banjo_deko3d_color_compression).
                                   Ryujinx ignores compression, so a compressed target sampled, copied or uploaded into wrongly
                                   is a console-only fault by nature. A little more GPU bandwidth; otherwise the same picture
  test11_no_shader_opts.toml       every shader optimisation off: the vertex-shader output pruning (an input the pixel shader reads
                                   that the pruned vertex shader no longer writes is garbage on the hardware and zero in Ryujinx:
                                   noise, black, blown-out patches are what that looks like) and uam's four passes. The shaders
                                   recompile on the console, so the first race is slow; the picture after that is the test
  test12_texture_dump_all.toml     test 9 widened: in four windows (120 s after launch, then every 40 s; one frame each) every
                                   texture any draw of that frame samples is copied out, up to 150 a window (about 40 MB each):
                                   the road, the scenery, the palms, the cables, the sky sprites, the tower's video, the car. A
                                   longer stall at each window. Be in a race with the bridge, palms and the tower in view from
                                   about 2.5 minutes after launch. Send texture_dump/ with the logs
  test13_everything.toml           all of the above at once, in one run (asked for 2026-11-04 07:15): tests 3-8, 10 and 11 switched
                                   the safe way plus test 12's whole-frame dump (windows from 3 minutes, every 45 s, four frames),
                                   but not test 2 (the clip plane off makes the car matte by design, so the chrome could not be
                                   judged). Slow: every barrier a full wait, copies off, shaders recompiled on the console, the
                                   game waiting on the render thread. If the car and the sky go right here, one of the switches
                                   is the cause and the next round halves them; if they stay wrong, every switch is ruled out in
                                   one go and the dump folder is the lead. Send logs/ and texture_dump/
  test14_range_path.toml           for the cables and the palm fronds drawn as ribbons across the sky in the course intro (your
                                   07:43 shots): those are triangle strips whose cuts the GPU is not honouring. This takes every
                                   draw through the path where the CPU keeps the cuts (banjo_renut_whole_buffers off; the fix of
                                   the earlier wedges lives there). If the intro's cables and fronds come right, that is the cause
                                   and the next build makes it the default on the console. Some CPU cost; watch the fps line
  test15_no_strip_restart.toml     the control for test 14: the GPU's primitive restart off altogether (banjo_deko3d_strip_restart).
                                   If the intro looks exactly as in the plain run, the restart was never taking effect on the
                                   hardware; if it looks worse, it was partly working. Run after test 14, not instead of it
If a test leaves the car exactly as it was, its keys are not the cause. If it clears the car, say which test, and I narrow it down.
Keep a copy of renut.toml first, to go back. Send logs/renut_001.log and logs/rex/rex_profile.log, and say which test each is from.
Whatever you run, the shipped renut.toml now writes a "[paint]" line a second per car-paint shader with the reflection constants the
game's code set for it (rr6_diag_paint_frames). Against the emulator's lines they tell CPU from GPU: the same values on the console
mean the GPU side (the reflection faces, the normal map, the blend); different values mean the game's code, and then test 3 is the one.

Which toml
----------
renut.toml        first run: shipped settings, logs on, CPU sampling on.
renut_play.toml   to play, diagnostics off.
renut_ab.toml     A/B: stay in one place for 10+ minutes, send logs/renut_001.log. Target 1 does nothing on the Switch: it is the control.

What to test, most important first
----------------------------------
1. Boot to a race. Logos, Pac-Man loader, title, World Xplorer, car select, first race.
2. Large wedge-shaped polygons: fixed by rr6_strip_markers (see above). If any are left, note where, and run renut_ab.toml: target 77's
   off half is the old behaviour.
3. Overall brightness. banjo_renut_game_gamma is now on: the display's gamma ramp, which the reference applies and Renut did not. Menus went
   from 3 to 12 levels off the reference to under 1. In renut_ab.toml it is target 73: the off half is visibly brighter in the darks.
4. Car reflections: the main thing to confirm. Fixed by rr6_user_clip_plane: the game's reflection map needs a clip plane Renut never applied.
   The car should look polished, with sky and scenery on the roof, spoiler, decals and glass, not matte. Matches the reference on the PC and in
   Ryujinx, but it relies on clip distances working on real deko3d, and only the console can prove that. In renut_ab.toml it is target 76:
   the off half turns the car matte, so a car that looks the same in both halves means the fix is not working on hardware. Tell me if so.
5. Glow on bright buildings. Fixed by rr6_fetch_over_pointer (target 75): the off half is about a quarter darker on lit surfaces.
6. Car at car select: should be textured. It was black until rr6_fog_nan_zero. Both worked in the emulator; confirm on hardware.
7. Tree flicker. Fixed by rr6_alpha_near_one (target 74). You confirmed it on the PC; the emulator's video could not show it on deko3d, so this
   is the first real look. Against it: older Xenia reports put side effects on a similar fix, so also check the checkpoint times' Pac-Man
   graphic and trees overlapping on corners.
8. Speed. The game slows down when frames run late: at about 38 fps in the emulator the lap clock ran at 0.755 of real time. It is not a
   strict one tick per frame. Compare the on-screen lap clock with a stopwatch in a race. The game's timing has not been changed.
9. Long stalls. The emulator had stretches under 3 fps around some loads and at the race's start, with no shader compiles: 3 to 7 windows of
   10 s in a run with the guard off, 7 to 12 with it on. Unknown whether this is the emulator. Note any stall on the console.
10. A dark scene with no car and the HUD bright, once in the emulator, while the car was stuck against the wall (emu11, capture 027). It looks
   like the game's own reset of a stuck car; not confirmed. Note it if you see it while driving normally.
11. Music: pick "Disc 4: Player Disc" under Change BGM, and race. Nobody has listened to this yet, on any platform. The largest pack
   (Silver Stream, 68.9 MB) opened and streamed on the PC. An old Xenia report says menu music stems do not loop: listen for that too.
12. Unlock keys: hidden by default. rr6_dlc_unlock_keys = true shows them; that is your decision.
13. Never tested here, from old Xenia reports: player 2 black in split-screen, replay saves, save names.

Machine copies
--------------
3,183 functions run as machine-optimised copies, up from 421. The NRO is 64.7 MB (35.6 before), with 1,734 MB of heap free in the emulator. Every one was checked on the PC against the generated code, with 0 differences:
- 3,043 were compared call by call with the original (557 million calls over two verify runs).
- 140 are a weaker class: functions a profile found hot, whose calls all reach something outside the copy, so they cannot be compared. They
  ran for real in guard-mode races, where nothing went wrong, but that is not a call-by-call proof. They include some of the hottest.
Functions my test runs never touched stay as generated code: correct, just not optimised. That covers anything those runs did not visit.
renut.toml has the guard off. To check on the console, use configs/renut_verify.toml and look for "[hot] DIFFERENCE" in the log: any such line
is a real finding, send it to me. banjo_cpu_native_bulk = false in renut.toml turns all the copies off, if you suspect them.

Console profile
---------------
renut.toml has switch_profile_stacks = true. Play the slow scene for a few minutes and send logs/rex/rex_profile.log with rr6-nx.elf from
this package: a profile only maps with the ELF of the same build. Sampling pauses threads 1,000 times a second, so read shares from such a
run, not its best frame rate. Name the scene and the time.

Not in this package, by your order: PGO and LTO, hand-written natives (they need a console profile first).

Known problems, not fixed
-------------------------
- PC only: Renut on Vulkan draws the race wrongly (the car's far side shows through, large polygons over the scene). Direct3D 12 and
  deko3d do not. Looks like a depth or stencil problem. Cause not found.
- PC only: Direct3D 12 hung the GPU twice (device removed, 887A0006), both times with another heavy process running.
- PC only: one stencil pipeline fails on Direct3D 12 (VS 05203E8E4637A806, PS BB976212FCEF91DA), so its draws are dropped.
- Direct3D 12 applies rr6_depth_bias only with the Agility SDK.
